card.statement:
Let $\lambda,\mu\in X_{*}(T)$ with $\lambda$ dominant.

We have

$\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}\cap T_{\mu}\neq\varnothing\ \Longleftrightarrow\ L_{\mu}\in\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \mu\in\mathop{\mathrm{Conv}}(W\lambda)\cap(\lambda+Q^{\vee}).$

If $\mu$ satisfies the condition in (1), the intersection $\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}\cap T_{\mu}$ has pure dimension $\langle\rho,\lambda-\mu\rangle$.

If $\mu$ satisfies the condition in (1), then $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}\cap T_{\mu}$ is open dense in $\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}\cap T_{\mu}$; in particular, the irreducible components of $\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}\cap T_{\mu}$ and $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}\cap T_{\mu}$ are in a canonical bijection.

5.3 Weight functors

Recall that if $X$ is a topological space, $i:Y\to X$ is the inclusion of a locally closed subspace and $\mathscr{F}\in D^{\mathrm{b}}_{c}(X,\mathbf{k})$, then the local cohomology groups $\mathsf{H}^{k}_{Y}(X,\mathscr{F})$ are defined as $\mathsf{H}^{k}(Y,i^{!}\mathscr{F})$.
card.label: Theorem 5.5

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
